key_insight: UniSlider makes image-editing sliders feel intuitive by mapping slider movement to perceptual change, not just raw model strength. This reduces dead zones, sudden jumps, and even reversals in the edited image.
problem_solved: Standard generative image-editing sliders are usually tied to a model’s internal strength parameter, which does not correspond well to how humans perceive change. As a result, slider motion often produces uneven, unpredictable, or non-monotonic visual edits.
method: Remap the underlying edit strength so equal slider steps produce more uniform perceptual changes in the output image.
Replace naive linear control with a perceptually calibrated slider behavior that better matches human expectations.
Improve the user experience of continuous image editing by making edits smoother, more consistent, and easier to control.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves the usability of image editing interfaces without changing the core generative model. It can make creative tools more reliable, interpretable, and practical for interactive workflows.

paper_title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing
